test_title: PYST 28: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - General Intelligence (Held On 4 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: reasoning
question:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All chairs are tables.

Some tables are stands.

All stands are baskets.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some chairs are stands.

II. Some tables are baskets.

III. All baskets are chairs.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.

solution:
From the given statements, the Venn diagram is:

All chairs are tables.

Some tables are stands.

All stands are baskets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/39989a4c4f76dbb09b6b02a9e6ad0cfea4ad1469f0eeaa7190c2f28b676b033d.png] 

Now we consider the given conclusions:

**I. Some chairs are stands: ** **does not follow**. [From the information given to us there is a relation between tables and stands & baskets and stands but we cannot assume the relation between chairs and stands, also from the diagram we can see that no chairs are stands and thus the conclusion does not follow.]

**II. Some tables are baskets: Follow [**Since some tables are stands and all stands are baskets so it will be correct to say that some tables are baskets due to the indirect relation present between them and therefore the conclusion follows.]

**III. All baskets are chairs: **does not follow ** [**From the given statement 'all stands are baskets.' we have the information which tells us the part of baskets region belongs to stands and tables but rest of the region is not related to any of the other classifications so we cannot assume about all baskets and thus the conclusion does not follow.]

Since only conclusion II follows.

Hence **the correct answer is option 2) **Only conclusion II follows.
